transcript: Last night I saw the Public's production of the Tempest at the Dela Court Theater in Central Park, and it was wonderful. The weather was beautiful, and we had a full moon. As part of the Public's annual Shakespeare in the park tradition, all tickets to the Tempest are free. I got mine by waiting in the standby line before the performance. Production is very unique. It's a 90 minute musical adaptation. It features an ensemble of dozens of New Yorkers from all five rows of the city, and it stars Rene Lee Schoolsbury as Prospero, her first stage role since Hamilton. I was a little skeptical of this casting choice going in, since prosper is traditionally a male character, but Renee really made the role her own, and I thought she was great. She's honestly a perfect actor for Shakespeare in the park, because sound can be an issue at an outdoor venue, and her diction is so crisp. I didn't find the material itself to be super groundbreaking, but it was really well performed, really fun, and the songs, which have lyrics in modern English, are helpful in conveying the plot. But what I really loved about the show is its community involvement. Really a love letter to New York City. This, combined with the free tickets, really epitomizes the idea of theater being by the people and for the people. If you're interested, the Tempest is running through this coming weekend in Central Park. With that another play Bill for My collection
